answer: After each epoch answer is posted, it remains in a public cooling window while established miners compute overlapping shingles of the text and file a collision flag if another answer shares too many n-grams or a matching nonce-gap pattern. Only a text that leaves that window without a confirmed cluster may receive a grading seat. Peers forge that collision record from ledger-visible shingles at settlement, so anyone can replay the count. A farm of near-copies fails the way a cheap violet pigment fails a batch assay: shared fragments group, and the whole cluster is refused together.
